research_question: Among women with a history of recurrent urinary tract infections (UTIs), what is the effect of cranberry products (juice, capsules, tablets, or powder, at any dose) versus placebo, no treatment, or another non-active control on the risk of having at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI during the longest on-treatment study follow-up?
treatment_label: Cranberry products (juice, capsules, tablets, or powder, at any dose)
control_label: Placebo, no treatment, or non-active control
outcome_description: Binary participant-level outcome: number of women with at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI during the full study period (longest follow-up on treatment) divided by the number analysed in each arm. Use the paper's primary UTI definition combining symptoms with a positive urine culture. Do not use episode counts, incidence rates, asymptomatic bacteriuria, bacteriuria alone, or symptoms-only definitions when a culture-verified definition is available. Prefer intention-to-treat denominators when reported; otherwise use the reported analysed sample and record which denominator was used. In multi-arm trials, combine eligible cranberry arms by summing participants and events; retain only eligible placebo/no-treatment/non-active control arms and ignore arms receiving other active agents.
positive_direction: A positive treatment effect means cranberry reduces the occurrence of symptomatic, culture-verified UTI relative to placebo, no treatment, or a non-active control (corresponding to RR < 1 before any direction harmonisation).
search_queries: cranberry recurrent urinary tract infection women randomized trial
cranberry juice capsules recurrent UTI placebo controlled women
cranberry symptomatic culture verified UTI women trial
inclusion_criteria: Randomised controlled trials enrolling women with a history of recurrent UTIs, including women who are currently infected or infection-free at baseline.
Trials comparing any cranberry product, formulation, or dose with placebo, no treatment, or another non-active control.

Trials reporting participant-level quantitative data for women with at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI during follow-up, with data sufficient to obtain events and totals for eligible arms.
exclusion_criteria: Not an original empirical randomised controlled trial, including systematic reviews, meta-analyses, editorials, opinion pieces, theoretical papers, protocols without results, and non-randomised studies.

No eligible comparison between cranberry and placebo, no treatment, or a non-active control; this includes cranberry-versus-antibiotic or cranberry-versus-probiotic studies with no eligible inactive control arm.

No quantitative participant-level outcome data that can produce an effect size: eligible arm totals and numbers of participants with at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI are unavailable; episode counts or incidence rates alone are insufficient and will not be converted to participant counts.

Completely unrelated to the research topic, or conducted exclusively in excluded populations such as children, pregnant women, institutionalised older people, or people with neurogenic bladder or urinary catheters.
moderators_to_extract: cranberry formulation (juice, capsule, tablet, or powder)
cranberry dose and proanthocyanidin content where reported
baseline infection status (currently infected versus infection-free)
recurrent-UTI eligibility definition and baseline UTI frequency
risk-of-bias domains, including allocation concealment, blinding, attrition, and outcome ascertainment
effect_size_note: Pool risk ratios (RRs) with a random-effects model using participants, not UTI episodes, as the unit of analysis. For each arm, extract the number of participants with at least one symptomatic, culture-verified UTI and the corresponding total. RR < 1 favours cranberry. Use intention-to-treat data when reported; otherwise use the analysed sample and explicitly record the choice. If several follow-up times are reported, use the cumulative outcome over the whole study period at the longest follow-up on treatment. For multi-arm trials, combine eligible cranberry arms by summing events and totals; use only eligible inactive-control arms, and omit active comparator arms. Do not substitute asymptomatic bacteriuria, adverse effects, adherence, dropouts, urinary E. coli counts, antibiotic use, bacteriuria-only outcomes, or symptoms-only outcomes when a culture-verified definition is reported. Report pooled RR with 95% CI, heterogeneity estimates (tau-squared and I-squared), study weights, and sensitivity analyses appropriate to risk of bias and sparse/zero-event data. Follow PRISMA 2020 for study identification, screening, exclusions, data extraction, risk-of-bias assessment, synthesis, certainty assessment, and reporting.
single_outcome_target: occurrence of symptomatic, culture-verified urinary tract infection
